outcome_analysis.explanation: The current completed official evaluations make this a both_pass pair: parallel and serial each passed 40 of 40 testcases. They converged on the same core solution, namely black-box inference of the single-wrap f32 hue-difference behavior plus custom C++ default-float formatting, then built and verified a Rust project. The concrete process difference is that parallel spawned a probe child and later interrupted it without consuming a returned result, while serial kept the same investigation and verification inside one thread.
parallel_contributors: Parent-side probing, implementation, builds, and 200 randomized comparisons were sufficient for the official pass.
The interrupted child created a parallel adverse lifecycle event but did not remove any required delivered behavior.
serial_contributors: The serial actor locally probed edge cases, implemented the same behavior, and verified with 1,000 randomized comparisons.
No delegation or handoff was needed for the serial solution.
ordinary_implementation_differences: Parallel used top-level color.rs and formatting.rs, while serial used src/color_space.rs and src/cpp_float.rs.
Parallel initially hit shell quoting errors in comparison scripts before a successful harness; serial avoided those specific harness errors.
evaluator_effects: Parallel cell/evaluation/summary.json is stale from an incomplete evaluator startup attempt; cell/status.json contains the completed retry that passed.
outcome_analysis.causal_scope: no outcome difference; one retained pattern is adverse process evidence only
